relations.subject: Otto von Böhtlingk
relations.evidence: Having studied (1833–1835) Oriental languages, particularly Arabic, Persian and Sanskrit, at the University of Saint Petersburg

relations.subject: Otto von Böhtlingk
relations.evidence: he continued his studies in Germany, first in Berlin and then (1839–1842) in Bonn.

relations.subject: Otto von Böhtlingk
relations.evidence: Returning to Saint Petersburg in 1842, he was attached to the Royal Academy of Sciences, and was elected an ordinary member of that society in 1855.

relations.subject: Otto von Böhtlingk
relations.evidence: His magnum opus was his great Sanskrit-German dictionary, Sanskrit-Wörterbuch... which with the assistance of his two friends, Rudolf Roth (d. 1895) and Albrecht Weber (b. 1825), was completed in 23 years.
